newsitem.title: USA: FPC Crystal River 3 shut pending NRC review.
newsitem.headline: FPC Crystal River 3 shut pending NRC review.

text.p: Florida Power Corp's (FPC) said Crystal River 3 nuclear generating unit would remain shut until the Nuclear Regulatory Commission (NRC) completes its safety review of a recent modification to part of the plant.
"The unit has to remain off line unit NRC reviews some findings...(on) a design issue with an emergency diesel generator," said company spokeswoman Karen Rahill.

The work performed on the generator would increase its electric power load, and NRC requested FPC for data pertaining to whether the modification would affect the overall safety level of Crystal River 3, NRC officials said.
"There's been no date established for the return of Crystal River unit 3 to service," Rahill said. "That (the modification issue) has to be resolved before the plant can be restarted."
She added it is unclear how much time the NRC would need to review the requested data on the modification.
Crystal River 3 was shut Sept 2 to replace a leaky section of a line that feeds lubrication oil to its turbine shaft. Replacement of the portion of the oil line was completed last week.

FPC, a subsidiary of Florida Progress Corp, is the operator and majority owner of the 825 megawatt Crystal River 3 power plant in Red Level, Fla. Ten Florida municipal utilities own the remaining interests in the unit.
